title: A published width slope gives no clear later tail prediction gain in eight other CHIME repeaters
abstract: We test a published pulse-width slope from FRB 20220912A on eight other CHIME repeaters. Each source level is fitted on early days. The fixed slope increases mean source log-tail squared error by 49.6 percent on 47 later bursts, after 42 early bursts. A day bootstrap gives an error-reduction interval from -169.3 to +4.5 percent. Five of eight sources have worse predictions. Single-component and high-signal cuts give no mean gain. The result does not establish a general failure of the slope. It limits a simple extension of one source relation. Shared fit errors, detection selection, few days and one instrument prevent a physical scattering claim. Original code, aggregate results, input hashes and retrieval steps are included. External record tables are excluded.

display.caption: Later prediction error for the fixed published width slope. Negative reduction means worse predictions. Controls keep the original source day splits.

citations.reason: Supplies the fixed slope. We test its transfer to other sources, which the prior work did not claim.
Supplies the earlier nine-source tail audit and sample context.
Shows sensitivity of tail interpretations to emission models.
